newsitem.title: USA: TWA waives advance purchase restrictions.
newsitem.headline: TWA waives advance purchase restrictions.

text.p: Major airlines geared up Friday for a possible strike at American Airlines, the nation's No. 2 carrier, waiving advance-purchase and other restrictions on discounted tickets and preparing to add flights.

United Airlines, Trans World Airlines Inc. and Continental Airlines Inc. said they would drop restrictions on discount tickets for customers who may be stranded by a pilots' strike at American, set for midnight Friday if no contract is reached.
Continental also said it was prepared to add flights and staff in key markets if American's pilots walk.

United, the No. 1 U.S. carrier, said it was offering discount one-way tickets Saturday through Monday. Joe Hopkins, a spokesman for the Chicago-based UAL Corp. unit, said it would waive restrictions on the tickets, which normally require advance purchase at least 14 days in advance. But the tickets are non-refundable.

TWA said passengers with American Airlines tickets bought before Feb. 15 can obtain a reservation on TWA, on the same city pair routing. The St. Louis-based airline said its waivers on discounted tickets would be effective through March 1.

Continental said it would increase flights between Dallas -- AMR Corp. unit American's back yard -- and the New York area and non-stop flights between the New York area and Los Angeles. The airline, based in Houston, also said it would increase staff at some locations.
Continental said it would accept unrestricted-fare tickets from American for any available seat in the comparable class of service on Continental for a similar routing between cities.
Passengers with discounted tickets from American, however, may have some restrictions. Continental said it is in talks with American on expanded ticket acceptance policies.
However, Continental said it had set a special fare for Feb. 15-17 allowing travelers to buy tickets for the 21-day advance purchase price.
Vanguard Airlines Inc. said it would offer one daily non-stop flight between Dallas/Fort Worth and Kansas City, Mo., in the event of a strike.
The Kansas City, Mo.-based airline said it could not accpet American Airlines or American Eagle tickets but would offer available seats at regular fares.
